description: You are a site administrator maintaining a user account management script for your website. The script, /home/user/user_manager.py, has recently been updated to fix a bug affecting how user IDs are handled. You want to perform a version bump and update the changelog to reflect this change. Here is what you need to do, step by step: 1. Update the project version in the file /home/user/version.txt. This file contains a single line with the current semantic version in the format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (for example, 1.0.2). Perform a patch bump: increase the PATCH number by one (e.g., from 1.0.2 to 1.0.3). 2. Edit /home/user/CHANGELOG.md to record the change. Append a new entry to the changelog with the new version number and the date of the update (use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format). The changelog entry must use this exact format (including the headings and bullet points): --- ## [NEW_VERSION] - YYYY-MM-DD - Fixed bug with user ID handling in user_manager.py --- Place the new entry at the end of CHANGELOG.md. 3. Verify your update by creating a log file called /home/user/version_update.log. This file should contain a single line summary in the exact format: Version bumped to NEW_VERSION on YYYY-MM-DD Where NEW_VERSION is the updated semantic version and YYYY-MM-DD is today's date. Automated tests will check: - /home/user/version.txt contains only the updated version number in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. - /home/user/CHANGELOG.md's last entry matches the specified format and today's date. - /home/user/version_update.log matches the specified summary format (single line, no extra whitespace or newlines). You have write access to these files and directories.
